newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia, Libya hold talks on energy cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia, Libya hold talks on energy cooperation.

text.p: Tunisia and Libya on Tuesday held talks on energy and fertiliser cooperation projects, Tunisian officials said.
Libyan Energy Minister Abdullah Salem al-Badri and Tunisian Industry Minister Slaheddine Bouguerra reviewed joint Tunisian Libyan projects in oil, gas, and electricity, they said.
They also decided to launch a joint project in fertilisers, the officials said without elaborating.

Tunisia and Libya set up in 1989 an oil company called Joint Oil to explore and exploit a shared offshore concession called "7 November", which has estimated recoverable oil between 211 million and 473 million tonnes.
The concession has also recoverable gas reserves estimated at between 132 billion and 328 billion cubic metres.

Last February, Tunisia and Libya reached an agreement to contract foreign companies to explore the concession, which is situated in the Gulf of Gabes, near the huge offshore Libyan oil field of Bouri.
Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi is also in Tunisia this week.
